questions.chapter: Machine Learning Models and Predictive Analytics
questions.text: Explain Logistic Regression for binary classification. Derive the Sigmoid activation function $\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$, odds ratio, and log-odds (logit) formulation. How does Binary Cross-Entropy loss penalize classification errors?
questions.solutionOutline: Maps linear combination z = w^T x + b into probability range [0, 1] using logistic function. Logit = ln(p/(1-p)) = w^T x + b. Model parameters optimized using maximum likelihood estimation via gradient descent on binary cross-entropy loss L = -[y ln p + (1-y) ln(1-p)].

questions.chapter: Machine Learning Models and Predictive Analytics
questions.text: Explain Decision Tree learning algorithm. Describe Information Gain, Shannon Entropy $H(S) = -\sum p_i \log_2 p_i$, and Gini Impurity criteria used by ID3 and CART algorithms to select best splitting attributes with a small numerical example.
questions.solutionOutline: Non-parametric supervised model building a tree of decision rules. ID3 uses Information Gain = Entropy(parent) - weighted Entropy(children). CART uses Gini Impurity = 1 - sum(p_i^2). High purity yields lowest entropy/gini; highest gain attribute selected at each internal split node.

questions.chapter: Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
questions.text: What is K-Means clustering? Explain the step-by-step algorithm, centroid update formula, convergence criteria, and the Elbow Method for determining optimal number of clusters ($k$).
questions.solutionOutline: Unsupervised partitioning algorithm. Steps: 1) Initialize k centroids randomly; 2) Assign each data point to nearest centroid using Euclidean distance; 3) Recompute centroid as mean of cluster members; 4) Repeat until centroids do not change or max iterations reached. Elbow method plots Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WCSS) vs k.

questions.chapter: Statistical Foundations and Probability Models
questions.text: Explain Hypothesis Testing in data science: Null Hypothesis ($H_0$), Alternative Hypothesis ($H_1$), significance level ($\alpha$), p-value, Type I error, and Type II error. When do we apply two-sample t-test versus z-test?
questions.solutionOutline: Statistical method to decide whether sample evidence supports rejecting H0. Type I error: rejecting true H0 (probability alpha). Type II error: failing to reject false H0 (probability beta). p-value <= alpha indicates statistical significance. Z-test used when population variance is known and n >= 30; t-test used when variance unknown and sample small.

questions.chapter: Machine Learning Models and Predictive Analytics
questions.text: What is Overfitting and Underfitting in supervised machine learning? Explain the Bias-Variance Tradeoff and describe regularization techniques: Ridge ($L_2$) and Lasso ($L_1$) regression penalty terms.
questions.solutionOutline: Underfitting: high bias, model too simple to capture patterns. Overfitting: high variance, model memorizes training noise failing to generalize. Ridge regression adds L2 penalty lambda * sum(w_i^2) shrinking weights smoothly. Lasso adds L1 penalty lambda * sum(|w_i|) driving unimportant coefficients to zero, performing embedded feature selection.

questions.chapter: Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization
questions.text: Differentiate between Correlation and Causation. Explain Pearson Correlation Coefficient ($r$) and Spearman Rank Correlation ($\rho$). How does a Correlation Heatmap assist in bivariate exploratory analysis?
questions.solutionOutline: Correlation measures statistical association; causation implies change in one variable directly produces change in another. Pearson r measures linear association between continuous variables: r in [-1, +1]. Spearman rho measures monotonic association using ranked data, robust to outliers. Heatmaps display pairwise correlation matrix using color gradients to spot collinear features.

questions.chapter: Data Preprocessing, Cleaning and Normalization
questions.text: What are Outliers in a dataset? Explain the Interquartile Range (IQR) method and Z-score method for detecting outliers. How should outliers be treated in data cleaning?
questions.solutionOutline: Outliers are data points deviating significantly from other observations. IQR method defines bounds [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR]. Z-score method flags data with |z| > 3. Treatment options: trimming/dropping (if data entry errors), winsorizing (capping at percentiles), or applying log transformations.

questions.chapter: Machine Learning Models and Predictive Analytics
questions.text: Explain Random Forest and Ensemble Learning methods. Compare Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregation) with Boosting (AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting) in terms of variance reduction and model accuracy.
questions.solutionOutline: Ensemble learning combines multiple base learners to achieve superior predictive accuracy. Bagging (Random Forest) trains diverse decision trees independently in parallel on bootstrap samples and random feature subsets to reduce variance. Boosting builds sequential trees where each subsequent tree corrects errors of predecessor, reducing bias.

questions.chapter: Introduction to Data Science and Roles
questions.text: Explain the Data Science Lifecycle according to the CRISP-DM methodology: Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Modeling, Evaluation, and Deployment.
questions.solutionOutline: Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM). 1) Business Understanding: formulate project goals and analytical problems; 2) Data Understanding: ingest, explore, assess quality; 3) Data Preparation: cleaning, transformation, feature engineering; 4) Modeling: select algorithms, tune hyperparameters; 5) Evaluation: validate against business metrics; 6) Deployment & Monitoring.

questions.chapter: Data Preprocessing, Cleaning and Normalization
questions.text: What is Categorical Data Encoding? Compare One-Hot Encoding and Label (Ordinal) Encoding. Why does One-Hot Encoding cause the curse of dimensionality on high-cardinality attributes?
questions.solutionOutline: Converts categorical strings into numerical format required by ML models. Label encoding assigns integer 0, 1, 2... suitable for ordinal data with intrinsic ranking. One-hot encoding creates binary column for each category, introducing high dimensionality and sparsity when cardinality is large, causing high memory and computation costs.

questions.chapter: Model Evaluation, Confusion Matrix and Cross-Validation
questions.text: Explain Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and Area Under Curve (AUC). How are True Positive Rate (Sensitivity) and False Positive Rate ($1 - \text{Specificity}$) plotted to compare classifier performance?
questions.solutionOutline: ROC curves plot TPR = TP/(TP+FN) on y-axis against FPR = FP/(FP+TN) on x-axis across varying classification threshold values from 1 to 0. AUC measures overall classification performance across all thresholds: AUC = 1.0 (perfect), AUC = 0.5 (random guess). Invariant to class imbalance.

questions.chapter: Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
questions.text: Explain Principal Component Analysis (PCA) step-by-step: data standardization, Covariance Matrix computation, Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors calculation, and projection onto principal components.
questions.solutionOutline: Unsupervised linear dimensionality reduction technique. Steps: 1) Standardize features to zero mean and unit variance; 2) Compute covariance matrix C = (1/n) X^T X; 3) Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors; 4) Sort eigenvectors in descending order of eigenvalues; 5) Form projection matrix W from top k eigenvectors; 6) Transform X_new = X * W.

questions.chapter: Data Ethics, Privacy and Emerging Trends
questions.text: Discuss Data Ethics, Algorithmic Bias, and Fairness in AI/Data Science. How can historical bias in training datasets lead to unfair discrimination in automated loan approvals and hiring systems?
questions.solutionOutline: Ethical considerations ensure responsible data handling. Algorithmic bias occurs when training data reflects societal prejudices or underrepresentation of minority groups. ML models perpetuate and amplify historical disparities. Mitigated through diverse training sets, fairness constraints (demographic parity, equal opportunity), and algorithmic auditing.

questions.chapter: Introduction to Data Science and Roles
questions.text: Explain Big Data characteristics through the 5 V's: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value. Differentiate between Batch Processing and Real-time Stream Processing architectures.
questions.solutionOutline: 5 Vs: Volume (massive dataset sizes), Velocity (high rate of data generation and ingestion), Variety (heterogeneous data formats: structured, text, video), Veracity (data quality and trustworthiness), Value (business actionable insights). Batch processing (Hadoop MapReduce) operates on large static historical data chunks; stream processing (Spark Streaming, Kafka) analyzes continuous real-time data events with sub-second latency.
